action_items: Priya Shah: Send pricing and 99th percentile latency table by 2026-12-29
Daniel Kim: Draft benchmark plan and test harness details by 2027-01-04

header:
Date: 2026-12-28 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Sara Li (Emberlytics CTO), Mark Rivera (Emberlytics ML Eng), Tom Bennett (Emberlytics Platform)
summary: Discovery focused on embeddings + reranking use case for Emberlytics' search product. Discussed vector DB integration, throughput, dimensionality, hybrid search, and deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private). Identified concerns around latency, cost, and data residency. Agreed next steps include pricing, security docs, and a benchmark plan.
transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Priya): hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Priya from Redwood, i'll hand over to daniel to kick off with quick agenda...
00:12 Speaker 2 (Daniel): thanks priya, yeah hi sara, mark, tom, good to meet you. quick agenda: 1) understand current infra and goals, 2) walk through embeddings + rerank flow, 3) constraints: latency/QPS/security, 4) next steps. sound good?
00:28 Speaker 3 (Sara): yep sounds good, thanks.
00:35 Speaker 2 (Daniel): cool so can you give us a quick picture of where you're at? production usage, vector store, sizes...
00:45 Speaker 3 (Sara): sure, so we're a knowledge search product for developer docs and customer support, so about 1.2M docs right now, we produce ~8-10M embeddings per month, storing them in a managed pinecone cluster - we've been hitting some spikes around high concurrency. QPS is usually 40-60 but peak can be 150 for short bursts.
01:05 Speaker 2 (Daniel): great, and what's your reranking setup? are you doing two-stage retrieval (ANN then cross-encoder rerank) or hybrid?
01:12 Speaker 4 (Mark): currently we do HNSW to retrieve top 100, then a BERT cross-encoder for rerank. It's CPU-heavy and we're seeing latency at the rerank step of 800-1200ms tail which kills UX.
01:30 Speaker 2 (Daniel): yep that's common. so our typical pattern is dense retrieval with embeddings (128-768 dims) + a lightweight reranker or tuned cross-encoder depending on quality needs. for throughput, important to know sequence length for cross-encoder and whether you can quantize.
01:50 Speaker 3 (Sara): right now embeddings are 512 dim. we experimented with 768 but cost jumped. we care about 95th and 99th percentile latency, ideally <200ms for initial recall and <400-500ms for full response.
02:12 Speaker 5 (Tom): also data residency - some docs are eu-only and we need audit logs and KMS.
02:22 Speaker 2 (Daniel): understood - we offer hosted regional endpoints, dedicated pools, and private (VPC) with customer-managed KMS. SOC2+, SSO via SAML, RBAC, and audit logs are available.
02:40 Speaker 3 (Sara): ok on the hosted vs dedicated question: what's the throughput difference? could you hit our peak of 150 QPS rerank with cross-encoder?
02:51 Speaker 2 (Daniel): short answer: yes, with Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; hosted can handle it too but you'd be on shared capacity so tails could vary. for cross-encoder rerank at that scale we'd recommend dedicated to keep p99 low.
03:10 Speaker 4 (Mark): can you share more on batching? would batching the cross-encoder help latency or hurt?
03:18 Speaker 2 (Daniel): batching helps throughput and GPU utilization but increases per-request latency unless it's continuous batching with strict latency SLOs. our runtime supports dynamic batching with latency-aware policies - so we can cap wait time to meet p95 targets.
03:40 Speaker 3 (Sara): how about vector DB: do you force customers to use pinecone or can we self-host FAISS/Weaviate?
03:48 Speaker 2 (Daniel): we integrate with all of those. you can keep Pinecone, or use self-hosted FAISS/Weaviate; many customers use FAISS locally for storage and route rerank through our Hosted/Dedicated runtime.
04:02 Speaker 4 (Mark): any recommendations on dimensionality? we've seen 512 good balance but open to lower dims if it helps cost.
04:10 Speaker 2 (Daniel): 128-512 tradeoffs: lower dims reduce index size and make ANN faster, but you may lose some recall. for many use cases 256 is sweet spot. we can run A/B on precision@k for your dataset.
04:30 Speaker 3 (Sara): what about hybrid search - combining BM25 with dense?
04:36 Speaker 2 (Daniel): hybrid is common - use BM25 for recall and dense embeddings to re-rank or we can combine scores. we also support hybrid retrieval in our guide; many customers run a BM25 prefilter to avoid embedding cost on obvious queries.
05:00 Speaker 4 (Mark): are embeddings for us generated by Redwood or do we bring our own?
05:06 Speaker 2 (Daniel): both - hosted API offers Redwood embeddings models; you can also bring embeddings precomputed from your models; we support consistent vector formats and dimensionality.
05:20 Speaker 3 (Sara): any tips on vector refresh and upserts? we expect high churn in docs.
05:27 Speaker 2 (Daniel): we support incremental upserts, and we have autoscaling shards for Dedicated. recommended pattern: upsert in batches and warm cache for hot docs.
05:40 Speaker 4 (Mark): security - KMS, customer-managed keys?
05:44 Speaker 2 (Daniel): yes, customer-managed KMS available on Private and Dedicated, and hosted with BYOK for enterprise; audit logs and exportable telemetry.
06:00 Speaker 3 (Sara): what's the pricing model specifically for embeddings + rerank?
06:06 Speaker 1 (Priya): pricing is usage-based for hosted (per-embedding unit + per-inference token), and reserved commitment for Dedicated. we'll send detailed sheet but rough order: embeddings charge per 1k vectors, rerank inference per 1000 requests; for Dedicated you get a flat hourly GPU cost.
06:30 Speaker 5 (Tom): we need to see 99th percentile tail numbers under load tests.
06:34 Speaker 2 (Daniel): absolutely - we can run a 100k vector + 10 QPS benchmark with your queries; will report p95/p99 and cost estimate.
06:45 Speaker 3 (Sara): what's the setup time for Private? could we get it in 6 weeks?
06:50 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Private deployment timelines vary; typical 6-10 weeks including infra and security review. Dedicated is faster - days to weeks.
07:05 Speaker 4 (Mark): crosstalk - interruption...
07:10 Speaker 5 (Tom): sorry one other: can we limit vector dimensionality via quantization to save memory?
07:15 Speaker 2 (Daniel): yes quantization and product-level 8-bit/4-bit formats are supported for inference and embeddings storage; depending on model you may lose minimal accuracy. we can recommend quant profiles.
07:32 Speaker 3 (Sara): are there managed connectors for S3/DBs to generate embeddings?
07:36 Speaker 1 (Priya): we have ingestion pipelines and SDKs for S3, GCS, and databases; can also integrate with your current pipeline.
07:48 Speaker 4 (Mark): what about multi-region? we'd need EU region for eu-data and US for us-data.
07:54 Speaker 2 (Daniel): supported - regional endpoints and can segregate data; Private gives strongest isolation.
08:05 Speaker 3 (Sara): great. could you email the security whitepaper and SOC2 cert?
08:09 Speaker 1 (Priya): yes will do.
08:12 Speaker 2 (Daniel): quick follow-up on reranker model: if you want lower latency we can suggest a distilled cross-encoder or a lightweight transformer for rerank; also consider pointwise models for some queries.
08:30 Speaker 4 (Mark): how does caching work for rerank?
08:34 Speaker 2 (Daniel): we can cache intermediate embeddings, and have prefix/KV caching for long sessions; rerank caching depends on query patterns but it's possible to cache results for repeated queries.
08:50 Speaker 3 (Sara): ok next steps?
08:54 Speaker 1 (Priya): recap: we'll send pricing and security docs, daniel will draft benchmark plan, schedule technical deep-dive with infra. agreed?
09:04 Speaker 3 (Sara): agreed, thanks.
09:10 Speaker 1 (Priya): thanks all, bye.
